# Coursework 1
# Part 2
# Task 1

#a. Load the dataset into a data frame

houseData = read.csv("house_sales(in).csv", header = TRUE)

#b. Report the total number of rows and columns of the data frame.

print('Number of columns: ')
print(ncol(houseData))
print('Number of rows: ')
print(nrow(houseData))

#c. List the column names

names(houseData)

#d. Keep the samples that have waterfront, view, and yr_renovated values <= 0

houseData <- houseData[houseData$waterfront <= 0, ]
houseData <- houseData[houseData$view <= 0, ]
houseData <- houseData[houseData$yr_renovated <= 0, ]

#e. Remove the following features: ``id", ``date”, ``waterfront", ``view",

drop <- c("id", "date", "waterfront", "view", "yr_renovated", "zipcode")

houseData <- houseData[,!(names(houseData) %in% drop)]


#f. Consider the price column as the target (y) and all other columns as features
#(X). Randomly shuffle the data, split it into two equal folds (almost), and
#rename them as train and test sets. 

#Shuffle the data randomly
set.seed(42) # For reproducibility
shuffled_houseData <- houseData[sample(nrow(houseData)), ]

#Find the midpoint split index
midpoint <- floor(nrow(shuffled_houseData) / 2)

#Split into equal train and test folds
train_set <- shuffled_houseData[1:midpoint, ]
test_set  <- shuffled_houseData[(midpoint + 1):nrow(shuffled_houseData), ]

#Separate features (X) and target (y)
X_train <- train_set[, !names(train_set) %in% "price"]
Y_train <- train_set$price

X_test  <- test_set[, !names(test_set) %in% "price"]
Y_test  <- test_set$price


# Task 2

#a. Select the statistically significant (alpha < 0.0001) features having the Spearman correlation coefficient (>= 0.30) with the price from the train set.


#Identify numeric feature columns
all_cols_train <- names(X_train)[sapply(X_train, is.numeric)]
target_cols_train <- setdiff(all_cols_train, "price")

#Test each column against price
ss_features_train <- c()

for (col in target_cols_train) {
  test_res <- suppressWarnings(
    cor.test(X_train[[col]], Y_train, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
  )

  rho <- test_res$estimate
  p_val <- test_res$p.value

  if (!is.na(p_val) && abs(rho) >= 0.30 && p_val < 0.0001) {
    ss_features_train <- c(ss_features_train, col)
  }
}

print(ss_features_train)

X_train <- X_train[, names(X_train) %in% ss_features_train, drop = FALSE]

#b. Choose the same set of features selected in 2 (a) from the test set.

all_cols_test <- names(X_test)[sapply(X_test, is.numeric)]
target_cols_test <- setdiff(all_cols_test, "price")

#Test each column against price
ss_features_test <- c()

for (col in target_cols_test) {
  test_res <- suppressWarnings(
    cor.test(X_test[[col]], Y_test, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
  )

  rho <- test_res$estimate
  p_val <- test_res$p.value

  if (!is.na(p_val) && abs(rho) >= 0.30 && p_val < 0.0001) {
    ss_features_test <- c(ss_features_test, col)
  }
}

print(ss_features_test)


X_test <- X_test[, names(X_test) %in% ss_features_test, drop = FALSE]

#c. Report the number of rows and columns of the train and test sets after steps 2 (a) and 2(b).

print('Number of columns: ')
print(ncol(X_train))
print('Number of rows: ')
print(nrow(X_train))

print('Number of columns: ')
print(ncol(X_test))
print('Number of rows: ')
print(nrow(X_test))
